verdict: Diamondback's revenue jumped 38% to $5.4B as oil fetched $87 a barrel and output rose, producing $2.1B of free cash flow and a higher dividend.

segments.name: Oil sales
segments.note: Crude oil — 48.3 million barrels sold at $87.30 a barrel on average.

segments.name: Sales of purchased oil
segments.note: Oil bought from others and resold — mostly passed through at cost.

segments.name: Natural gas liquids
segments.note: Liquids separated from gas — 24.3 million barrels at $20.02 a barrel.

segments.name: Natural gas sales
segments.note: Gas — 135 billion cubic feet at $1.12 per thousand cubic feet.

opex.name: Depreciation, depletion & amortization
opex.note: The wearing-out cost of wells and equipment — a non-cash charge.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — head office and staff.

otherDetail: A $182M loss on commodity derivative contracts (price hedges), $55M of net interest expense and $5M of other income, plus a $4M gain on buying back debt below face value, net.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $3.51 a year ago; adjusted EPS $5.86

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: cash left after drilling and building

kpis.label: Oil production
kpis.note: 1,034K barrels of oil equivalent per day in total

takeaways.title: Price did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: Diamondback sold its oil for $87.30 a barrel, up from $64.60 a year ago. With output up about 10% to 1,034 thousand barrels of oil equivalent a day, revenue rose 38%.

takeaways.title: Cash poured out of the ground
takeaways.text: Free cash flow — operating cash minus drilling and building — was $2,148M. The company returned $582M to shareholders and raised the base dividend 7.3% to $1.18 a share.

takeaways.title: Hedges capped the upside
takeaways.text: Price-hedge contracts lost $182M in the quarter: when oil rises above the hedged price, the hedge pays out. It is the cost of the insurance that protects Diamondback when prices fall.

oneTimers: A $182M loss on derivative instruments (hedges) is included in other expense above; adjusted net income of $1,649M ($5.86 per share) excludes it and similar items.
Diamondback bought back $106M of its 2054 and 2064 bonds below face value, booking a $4M gain on debt extinguishment.

sources.label: Official earnings release (Globe Newswire, as filed on SEC EDGAR 8-K Ex. 99.1)

footerNote: Energy format: direct costs are lease operating expenses, production and ad valorem taxes, gathering/processing/transportation and the cost of purchased oil resold. Oil, gas and NGL sales are split using the release's sold volumes and realized prices (they sum to the reported $4,854M of oil, gas and NGL sales). Net income of $1,771M is the total before $168M attributable to non-controlling interests (mainly Viper Energy); $1,603M was attributable to Diamondback shareholders.
